coverage.assessment: The essential steps of the theory survive. The revision removed the 'stumbling-block' that the cutting solves, the disfigured body that links the cutting to Julius, and the bribe that triggered exposure. Each step is now asserted rather than reasoned. The staged-rescue 'put-up job' rationale is also gone.

'get him out of the way' now lacks its immediate antecedent, because the clause about Beresford being in the neighbourhood was cut. Entrances, the curtain, the prison room, the treaty's pocket-book location and the seizure from behind are otherwise clear.

Tuppence's 'But I can't see _why!_' became narrated summary, so Sir James's 'Can't you? I can.' answers a line no longer spoken. The rest of the turn-taking and attribution, including Julius's drawl and the gaze on Tommy, is intact.
Hedges such as 'probably', 'I rather fancy' and 'almost swear' survive where kept. The theory remains Sir James's assertion, not narrated fact.
There is no premature disclosure. The revision did cut Tuppence's footstep and creaking cues, which built her limited-knowledge suspense and faintly signalled the hidden rescuers.
The climax keeps its exact pacing. Several ironic, exclamatory beats that precede the reversal are trimmed: 'They were going to win!', 'No dummy this time!', and 'he will not find us unprepared'.

Two ironies that turn on the impersonation are lost. One is 'Mr. Brown is a consummate actor', said by the actor himself. The other is Tuppence's comfort that police would break in, which is precisely his plan.
All three dependencies are intact at both endpoints in the revised drafts of 025 and 028.

strengths: The unmasking-to-death sequence (revised paragraphs 31–46) is preserved essentially verbatim. This includes the 'In this room....' pacing, the 'three, not two' gloat, the gaze on Tommy, Ave Caesar and the bitter almonds.

All continuity checks hold. The theory stays in Sir James's speech, the 'No one has gone into the house' claim is retained, the treaty goes into his pocket-book, and the source typo is corrected to 'Mr. Brown'.
Jane's essential line 'Those papers were my trust' and the Marguerite recovery, with its magazine-page mechanism, remain clear.
summary: The revision keeps the plan's architecture intact. Sir James's theory stays in speech, the curtain fancy survives, the police claim and the pocket-book are retained, and all verbatim lines and the unmasking-to-death sequence are preserved exactly with no 'Bown'. The revision (not the first draft) cut further into connective tissue. That leaves one loosely anchored pronoun and a reply to a dropped question. It also thins the logic of the impersonation theory and removes several ironies that the reversal depends on, chiefly Tuppence's reassurance that the police would break in. None of these is a blocker; all are small, source-grounded repairs.
